To: posts/new
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Correction: GST formula in the daily takings template

I need to correct an error in the daily takings and GST template I shared in August.

The error is mine. I am sorry. People used the sheet knowing I am an accountant, and Melvin is right to be upset that he trusted it. Thank you to Ravi and Shu Fen for catching the mistake and bringing it to my attention.

What went wrong

In versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2, the formula in column F multiplied daily takings by 9%. That is wrong when the takings entered already include GST. To find the GST portion of a GST-inclusive amount, the formula should use 9/109.

Ravi’s example makes this clear. His takings were $1,090 including GST. The sheet showed $98.10 in GST; the correct amount is $90. That is a difference of $8.10.

I tested version 1.0 against my own sample figures before sharing it. Those figures were already excluding GST, so the check passed and I missed the problem. I should have tested inclusive takings as well.

Who is affected

This affects anyone who entered GST-inclusive takings in versions 1.0, 1.1 or 1.2. I know that will include many hawkers. If all the amounts you entered excluded GST, this particular formula error does not affect those entries.

There have been 412 downloads since 12 August. The error overstates GST on inclusive takings; it does not cause an underpayment to IRAS. It does mean some of you may have overpaid and need to check how to correct it.

The quarterly Box 1 sales total was calculated separately and was correct. The error affected the Box 6 GST figure.

What to do now

I uploaded the corrected version, v1.3, on 8 November. Please download it from the original post and stop using versions 1.0 to 1.2.

In v1.3, check cell H2 before entering your takings. Choose “prices exclude GST” only if the amounts you enter exclude GST. If your receipts include the GST collected, use the inclusive setting, even if your menu prices are shown excluding GST.

If you have already filed your July–September return using the sheet, please:

1. Keep a copy of the old sheet and your filed return. Do not overwrite your records.
2. Check which version you used and whether the takings you entered included GST.
3. If they did, use v1.3 with the inclusive setting in H2 to recalculate the GST for the quarter. Compare that result with the Box 6 figure you filed, and keep a record of the difference.
4. Check the IRAS page on correcting GST errors and speak to the person who files your GST returns, if you have one. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error can go into a later F5 or needs a GST F7. Please check the appropriate route before making a correction.

If you have not filed yet, use the corrected sheet and check your figures before submitting. If you are unsure about your return or how to correct it, check with IRAS or your filer.
